correctness.rationale: For the independent exponential waits and independent restart decisions, from a fresh state zero the probability of reaching k is s_k and that of never resetting is q_beta. The latter is positive exactly when beta>1 by the infinite-product criterion. In this case the first infinite-growth excursion occurs after a geometric number of failures; its total wait has finite mean tau/(1-r). Otherwise infinitely many fresh state-zero waits force divergence almost surely. Regeneration and Tonelli give the mean B_beta/q_beta with B_beta=tau sum r^k s_k. In log q_beta, the first log-series term -c zeta_R(beta) yields the pole and -c EulerGamma, and the m>=2 terms are dominated by zeta_R(2)c^m/m. The finite part is -log Gamma(1-c). Dominated convergence and the binomial generating function give B_beta -> tau(1-r)^(c-1). For the limit law, condition on the geometric failure count G. Failure durations can be drawn i.i.d. independently of G with the conditional failure law; their variances are bounded as q_beta->0 because each unconditioned excursion is dominated by the full geometric sequence of waits with finite second moment. Thus the centered sum of failure durations multiplied by q_beta tends to zero in L2, since q_beta^2 E[G]=O(q_beta). The conditional failure mean tends to the positive limit of B_beta, the final success cost vanishes after scaling, and q_beta G converges to Exp(1). This also independently checks the renewal Laplace proof. The support checker and VERIFICATION.md were inspected but not executed; the finite depth and numerical checks do not certify these limits. The asymptotics fix c,r,tau, and no post-accumulation continuation is asserted.

value.rationale: The minimum question in an accelerating internal-renewal walk is whether its departure clock stays finite. The summability boundary answers that question and the explicit finite prefactor calibrates how long an almost-sure accumulator can look nonexplosive just above threshold. Together with the limiting law this gives a useful quantitative time scale rather than just an explosion example or an order-of-magnitude estimate.
